Every line of src/NCode.Randomness/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt and PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, and of the same files of NCode.Randomness.Curby, NCode.Randomness.Nist and NCode.Randomness.Drand, is in exactly one entry's api, which build/Assert-ApiMap.ps1 checks. entries.summary: A cryptographically secure random source: its bytes are unpredictable to everyone, so they suit keys, secrets, tokens, salts and nonces. It adds no member to `IRandomSource`; it is a capability that the type system checks.
Produces uniformly distributed random bytes. Every typed value, range, shuffle and selection in this library is built on this one operation.
Fills `destination` with random bytes. An empty buffer is left as it is.
The operating system's cryptographically secure random number generator as an `ISecureRandom`. Use it wherever no beacon is wanted, such as in an air-gapped deployment.
The shared instance. The type is stateless and thread-safe, so the one instance serves every caller, and it needs no disposal.
Fills `destination` with bytes from `RandomNumberGenerator`.
Typed values, ranges, shuffles and selections over any `IRandomSource`. Every member is unbiased, and deterministic given the source's bytes.

The secure generator, the background beacon collection and reproducible draws, composed without dependency injection, for console tools and libraries that run without a host. Keep one instance for the life of the application.

Creates a builder with default options, options set by `configure` or options bound from `configuration`. An unknown configuration key fails `BuildAsync`, so a misspelled setting is never silently ignored.
Gets the secure generator.
Gets the health of the beacon collection.
Gets the factory for reproducible draws.
Stops the beacon collection, waiting up to 30 seconds, and disposes the generator, zeroing its state. A second call does nothing.
Composes a `RandomnessHost`: add beacons with the adapters' extension members, such as `AddCurbyBeacon()`, then call `BuildAsync` once.
Gets the services the host is built from. Add what a host would add, such as a logging provider; a registration made after `BuildAsync` has no effect.
Builds the host: checks every setting, as a host does at start, and starts collecting beacon pulses in the background. With `RequireInitialPulse` set, it waits for the first pulse.
Settings for the secure generator and the beacon collector, bound from the `Randomness` configuration section.
The configuration section these options bind from by convention.
How the registered beacons are used. The default is `BeaconMode.Continuous`.
How often each beacon is asked for its latest pulse. The default is one minute, the cadence at which CURBy publishes.
The longest wait between attempts while a beacon fails; the wait doubles from `RefreshInterval` up to it, with jitter. The default is fifteen minutes.
How long one attempt to fetch a pulse may take. The default is thirty seconds.
The oldest a pulse may be, by its own timestamp, to be mixed in; an older one means a beacon or a mirror has stalled. The default is ten minutes.

signatures: public Dictionary<string, TimeSpan> MaxPulseAgeByBeacon { get; set; }
entries.summary: The oldest a pulse may be, by beacon name, in place of `MaxPulseAge`, for a beacon that publishes less often. A name that no registered beacon has fails the host at start. Empty by default.
How far a pulse's timestamp may lie ahead of this machine's clock. The default is two minutes.
Whether the host fails to start unless a beacon pulse is mixed in within `InitialPulseTimeout`. The default is `false`: a beacon outage never stops an application.
How long the host waits at start for the first pulse when `RequireInitialPulse` is set. The default is thirty seconds.
The longest any generator shard runs before it reseeds from the operating system. The default is one minute.
The most bytes any generator shard produces before it reseeds from the operating system. The default is one mebibyte.

How the library uses the registered randomness beacons. `Continuous` fetches at start and every `RefreshInterval`, `InitializeOnly` fetches until each beacon has given one pulse, and `Offline` contacts no beacon. In every mode, random values are generated locally and never wait on a beacon.

A public randomness beacon, such as CURBy: the port each vendor's adapter implements. An implementation verifies every pulse as its vendor's protocol specifies before it returns it, and throws `BeaconException` rather than return a pulse it could not verify.
Gets the name the beacon is registered under, unique among the registered beacons, such as `curby`.
Fetches and verifies the beacon's latest pulse. It throws `BeaconException` when the beacon gave no verifiable pulse.
Fetches and verifies the pulse of `round`. It throws `BeaconException`, with `BeaconError.PulseNotFound` when the round has not been published.

entries.summary: Registers the CURBy-Q beacon, named `curby-q`, with its default options (the CURBy-Q and Bell chains served by `CurbyDefaults.BaseAddress`), options set by `configure` or options bound from `configuration`. It allows `curby-q` pulses up to 30 minutes old, unless `Randomness:MaxPulseAgeByBeacon:curby-q` or a longer `Randomness:MaxPulseAge` is set.
The CURBy beacon's published identifiers.
The name the CURBy beacon is registered under: `curby`.

The content identifier of the CURBy-RNG chain, the beacon's randomness chain, which publishes a pulse every minute. A content identifier is the hash of the chain's document, which holds the chain's signing key, so pinning it pins the key: no server, mirror or TLS certificate can substitute another.
The name the CURBy-Q beacon is registered under: `curby-q`.

The content identifier of the CURBy-Q (DIRNG) chain, whose rounds publish randomness extracted from a loophole-free Bell test. A content identifier is the hash of the chain's document, which holds the chain's signing key, so pinning it pins the key.
The content identifier of the Bell chain, on which the Bell experiment answers each CURBy-Q request with the hash of its data. Pinning it pins its signing key.
The base address of the HTTP API that serves CURBy's Twine chains.
The name of the `HttpClient` the beacon uses, for a host that adds its own handlers, such as a proxy, with `services.AddHttpClient(CurbyDefaults.HttpClientName)`.

Settings for the CURBy and CURBy-Q beacons, which share them, bound from the `RandomnessBeacons:Curby` configuration section, beside the `Randomness` section of the core options, whose strict binding refuses any key it does not know.
The configuration section these options bind from by convention.

The base address of the Twine HTTP API, an absolute `https` URL ending in `/`, with no user info, query or fragment. The default is `CurbyDefaults.BaseAddress`. A mirror serves the same data: every document is verified against `ChainId`, so a mirror can withhold pulses but never forge one.
The content identifier of the chain to trust. The default is `CurbyDefaults.RngChainId`.
The content identifier of the CURBy-Q chain to trust. The default is `CurbyDefaults.QuantumChainId`.
The content identifier of the Bell chain to trust, on which the Bell experiment answers each CURBy-Q request. The default is `CurbyDefaults.BellChainId`.
The largest response body read, in bytes. The default is 256 KiB; a pulse is about 4 KiB.
How long a failed chain fetch is remembered: until it passes, a pulse on that chain fails at once, without another request. The default is 1 minute; it must be from 1 second to 1 day.

Verifies CURBy-RNG pulse documents that a caller supplies, without the network, by every check the CURBy beacon makes: chain, pulse and predecessor each hash to their CIDs and are signed by the chain's key, the predecessor is one round earlier, and the pulse's salt matches its precommitment. An instance is immutable and thread-safe.

It throws `BeaconException` when a document is malformed or missing, the round has no randomness, or any check fails.

entries.summary: Registers the NIST beacon, named `nist`, with its default options (chain 2 of the NIST Randomness Beacon 2.0 served by `NistDefaults.BaseAddress`, verified against the certificates of `NistDefaults.CertificateIds`), options set by `configure` or options bound from `configuration`, such as `configuration.GetSection("RandomnessBeacons:Nist")`. An unknown configuration key fails the host at start.
The NIST Randomness Beacon's published identifiers.
The name the NIST beacon is registered under: `nist`.
The base address of the NIST Randomness Beacon 2.0 HTTP API.
The index of the chain the beacon trusts: chain 2, which publishes a pulse every minute.
The name of the `HttpClient` the beacon uses, for a host that adds its own handlers, such as a proxy, with `services.AddHttpClient(NistDefaults.HttpClientName)`.

The identifiers, oldest first, of the certificates NIST signs chain 2 with. An identifier is the SHA-512 hash of a certificate's DER encoding in lowercase hex, so pinning it pins the certificate and its key: no server, mirror or TLS certificate can substitute another.

Settings for the NIST beacon, bound from the `RandomnessBeacons:Nist` configuration section, beside the `Randomness` section of the core options, whose strict binding refuses any key it does not know.
The configuration section these options bind from by convention.

The base address of the NIST HTTP API, an absolute `https` URL ending in `/`, with no user info, query or fragment. The default is `NistDefaults.BaseAddress`. A mirror serves the same data: every pulse is verified against the pinned certificates, so a mirror can withhold pulses but never forge one.
The index of the chain to trust. The default is `NistDefaults.ChainIndex`.

The identifiers of the certificates to trust, each the SHA-512 hash of a certificate's DER encoding in hex. When empty, the default, `NistDefaults.CertificateIds` applies; a configured list replaces the defaults.

How long a failed certificate fetch is remembered: until it passes, a pulse that names the certificate fails at once, without another request. The default is 1 minute; it must be from 1 second to 1 day.
The largest response body read, in bytes. The default is 64 KiB; a pulse is about 2 KiB.

Verifies NIST Randomness Beacon 2.0 pulse documents that a caller supplies, without the network, by every check the NIST beacon makes: the pinned chain and certificate, the certificate's hash, key size and validity, the pulse's version, cipher suite, signature and output value, and the predecessor's index, time, hash link and precommitment. An instance is immutable and thread-safe.

entries.summary: Verifies a pulse and its predecessor and returns the pulse as the NIST beacon returns it. Each document is as the NIST API serves it: the pulses in UTF-8 JSON, the certificate as PEM. The first overload takes one `certificate`, for a predecessor that names the same certificate; the second takes a `predecessorCertificate` too, as across a certificate rotation. It throws `BeaconException` when a document is malformed or any check fails.

The name the drand beacon is registered under: `drand`.
The base address of the drand HTTP API.
The hash of the quicknet chain, in lowercase hex: its identifier in the HTTP API.
The quicknet chain's pinned group public key: a compressed G2 point in lowercase hex. Every round is verified against it, so no server or mirror can substitute another.
The time of round 1, in Unix seconds.
The seconds between rounds.
The name of the `HttpClient` the beacon uses, for a host that adds its own handlers, such as a proxy, with `services.AddHttpClient(DrandDefaults.HttpClientName)`.

Settings for the drand beacon, bound from the `RandomnessBeacons:Drand` configuration section, beside the `Randomness` section of the core options, whose strict binding refuses any key it does not know.
The configuration section these options bind from by convention.

The base address of the drand HTTP API, an absolute `https` URL ending in `/`, with no user info, query or fragment. The default is `DrandDefaults.BaseAddress`. A mirror serves the same data: every round is verified against the pinned group key, so a mirror can withhold rounds but never forge one.
The largest response body read, in bytes. The default is 16 KiB; a round is about 200 bytes.

Verifies drand quicknet round documents that a caller supplies, without the network, by every check the drand beacon makes: the round's signature must be a point of G1 other than the identity and verify against the pinned group public key for the round number, and a `randomness` member, when present, must be the SHA-256 of the signature. An instance is immutable and thread-safe.

Verifies a round against the pinned chain and returns it as the drand beacon returns it. `round` is the round document, as the drand API serves it, in UTF-8 JSON. It throws `BeaconException` when the document is malformed or a check fails.
